correctness.rationale: For two equal instantaneous impulses and identical 4-stage Nash kernels, after dimensionless scaling G_tau(x)=x^3e^{-x}+1_{x>=tau}(x-tau)^3e^{-(x-tau)}. For x>tau, e^x G_tau prime is cubic P_tau=x^2(3-x)+e^tau(x-tau)^2(3-x+tau), with symbolic discriminant exactly -108 tau^2 e^{2tau} F(tau), F=6cosh(tau)-2tau sinh(tau)+6-3tau^2+tau^4/4. The series of F prime has a strictly negative polynomial upper bound for all positive tau, F(2)>0>F(3), giving unique tau*=2.95880814824387897254... . For 0<tau<3, all cubic real roots lie in (3,3+tau), discriminant sign counts one simple root vs three simple roots, and at equality one double stationary shoulder and one simple maximum. At tau>=3 the original impulse has its peak at x=3, while two post-arrival stationary roots add one local minimum and one maximum. Independent SymPy symbolic discriminant identity and high-precision root/sign classification reproduced the transition; finite root samples corroborate only the analytic sign proof.

value.rationale: For the classical four-stage linear-reservoir impulse response, delayed equal inputs create a genuine mode-bifurcation. The exact dimensionless separation threshold and shoulder boundary provide an interpretable analytical benchmark for sequencing in idealized hydrologic response, beyond simply knowing the gamma hydrograph formula. The result does not assert operational real-flood safety or global peak dominance.

limitations: Identical four-reservoir linear cascades, equal instantaneous pulses and common rate k only; claim concerns count of strict local maxima not floods in physical catchments.
